Subject: SlateBridge renewal + capacity realignment request

Hi Evelyn / Ben —

We're coming up on our annual renewal (deal D-74291) and wanted to flag a material change in how we've been consuming Dedicated capacity. Over the past 8 weeks our inference traffic for real-time ranking has sustained a much higher tail: 95th percentile token throughput has increased ~2.3x versus what we forecasted during the initial commit. Attached is our July usage export; the key points:

- Current committed pool: 80x "V100-equivalent" slots (mixed coeff).
- Observed steady p50 load is ~65 slots, but p95 regularly spikes to 140+ concurrent device-equivalents for short windows (30s-5m).
- Cost sensitivity: we need to keep committed units reasonable, but avoid user-impacting throttling.

We're exploring either adding short-term GPUs to cover the new tail or switching to a mixed plan (smaller base commit + burst credits + a small pool of A100s for high-efficiency signals). Can Redwood provide a sizing proposal and operational plan that minimizes app risk and gives us a clear path at renewal?

Looking for a quick rundown and an estimate for: 1) size to commit today to avoid degradation, 2) a tiered rollout plan (canary -> scale), 3) timeline & procurement steps so we can sync with internal finance.

Best,
Alex
Head of ML Platform
SlateBridge

Attachments: SlateBridge_usage_report_July2026.csv (CSV, 2.1MB)

From: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: SlateBridge renewal + capacity realignment request

Alex — thanks for the upload and the crisp summary. We saw the same pattern in our observability dashboard and I appreciate you surfacing the p95 behavior explicitly. High level we can approach this two ways:

Option A — Stability-first (short-term): add a tranche of dedicated devices to cover current tail (recommend +40 device-equivalents as a stopgap), keep existing commit, then run a 6-week utilization assessment. Pros: immediate relief. Cons: higher short-term committed cost.

Option B — Flex-forward (recommended for cost/efficiency): rebaseline to a 60-device commit comprised of higher-efficiency A100-equivalents + a 40-device burst buffer (on-demand/burst credits) and an autoscale policy that aggressively uses prefix/KV caching and short-window pre-warming to reduce peak memory load. Pros: lowers steady-state cost and reduces thermal headroom. Cons: needs a controlled rollout and slight engineering changes.

To get you a binding SOW and timeline: can we set a short call tomorrow? Also looping in Kim (cc) for the technical sizing sketch and a rough pricing delta.

Evelyn Hart
Director, Dedicated Accounts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SlateBridge renewal + capacity realignment request — technical proposal

Alex / team — ran the telemetry and put together a technical plan aligned to Option B (flex-forward) with operational mitigations. Summary:

- Proposal: Commit 60 A100-equivalent dedicated devices + purchase a 40-device burst credit pool (30-day replenishing).
- Rationale: Observed p50 ~65 (so 60 commit is slightly conservative) while bursts can be handled by burst credits. A100-equivalents improve throughput per device (~1.6x vs V100).
- Autoscale/Runtime changes: enable short-window proactive pre-warm for 15s windows on top offender routes, set continuous batching thresholds to 12ms, and enable prefix KV caching for the session types that are heavy on repeated prompts. These changes should reduce p95 device-equivalent by ~18% in our sim.
- Rollout: week 0 — deploy burst credits and apply autoscale policy to 5% of traffic (canary); week 1–3 — expand to 30% then 100% if metrics show stability; week 6 — final commit amendment executed if telemetry meets SLO.
- Cost delta (rough): +24% monthly vs current committed costs if SlateBridge keeps a 12-month term but reduces baseline device count; with 12-month commitment discount applied, net increase vs current spend expected ~+8% while reducing throttling risk to near-zero.

I'll attach a short SLO template and a draft amendment we can hand to procurement. Evelyn — if you want I can mock the amendment numbers into Ben's sketch and produce a customer-ready SOW.

Kimberly Park
Solutions Lead, Redwood Dedicated
